title: Case split on the typeP-pair dichotomy for no_minSimple_odd_group
intent: Record the last step of the Feit-Thompson theorem — the contradiction `no_minSimple_odd_group` that rules out a minimal simple group of odd order — as a theorem-scale decomposition whose 37-line glue proof is nothing but an exhaustive case split (`FTtypeP_pair_cases`), a `without loss` ordering `q < p`, one `have := <named project lemma>` per fact, and a single final application of `FTtype2_exclusion`.

Lemma typeP_pair_sym S T W W1 W2 (defW : W1 \x W2 = W) (xdefW : W2 \x W1 = W) :
  typeP_pair S T defW -> typeP_pair T S xdefW.

  typeP_pair S T defW -> exists U : {group gT}, of_typeP S U defW.

Lemma FTtypeII_support_facts T L (Q := T`_\F) (H := L`_\F) :
    FTtype S == 2%N -> typeP_pair S T defW -> L \in 'M('N(U)) ->
  [/\ (*a*) [Frobenius L with kernel H],

    & (*c*) H ><| W1 = L \/ (exists2 y, y \in Q & H ><| (W1 <*> W2 :^ y) = L)].

applicability.goal_shape: An impossibility theorem `forall gT, C gT -> False` discharged by reducing `C` to a finite, exhaustive dichotomy — either every object is of a small kind, or a distinguished pair exists — where each arm closes by a named lemma and the remaining hypotheses concentrate onto the pair.
applicability.use_when: the dichotomy is already a proved project lemma (stated as a `\/` or a classification), both arms close by named lemmas, and a symmetry (`without loss`/`wlog`) lets one ordering stand for both branches.
applicability.avoid_when: the split's exhaustiveness is not yet proved (then the disjunction is itself a child with its own obligation — survey F rule 5); the arms need non-uniform arguments that do not factor through named lemmas; or the final lemma takes a long positional argument list that any reshuffling of intermediate facts would break.

claims.claim: Each of the 12 lemmas the glue applies directly — FTtypeP_pair_cases, not_all_FTtype1, typeP_pair_sym, typeP_pairW, FTtypeP_max_typeII, FTtypeP_min_typeII, compl_of_typeII, FTtypeII_support_facts, FT_Frobenius_type1, FTtype1_coherence, FTtype1_ref_irr, FTtype2_exclusion — is a closed Lemma/Theorem/Fact/Remark ending in `Qed.` at the pinned commit, none an axiom, hypothesis or admitted.

consequences: The split creates two obligations (the left and right arms of the `\/`); the exhaustiveness is carried by FTtypeP_pair_cases itself, so the parent never re-proves it. Inside the right arm a `without loss q < p` swaps S/T and W1/W2 via typeP_pair_sym, so one ordering stands for both. The final FTtype2_exclusion is applied to a 16-argument positional list assembled purely by `have := <lemma>`; if any intermediate fact changes shape (e.g. FTtypeII_support_facts returning a different conjunction), the single `exact:` call breaks.
